_note: Golden cross-language fixtures for the lock-state contract, consumed by BOTH scripts/lock-math-test.mjs (src/shared/lock-math.ts) and the smartblocker-core cargo tests (lock_math.rs / merge.rs). Every case here must pass identically in TypeScript and Rust — that is the parity guarantee between the extension and the desktop companion. Schedule rules pinned to `tzOffsetMinutes` evaluate against that FIXED offset regardless of the host zone, so the tz-pinned cases below are host-independent by design (red-team #26); UNPINNED rules still follow the device's current zone, which the Rust runner pins to Utc and the TS runner leaves local — legacy-window behavior is therefore covered by each language's own unit tests instead of this file. The DST-residual case documents the accepted cost of fixed-offset pins: a rule pinned on winter time fires one hour off the civil clock after a DST change (the mirror has no IANA tz database — offline build constraint). The merge runner additionally asserts commutativity (merge(b,a) == expect) and idempotence (merge(expect,expect) == expect) for every case. `reasons` array order is fixed: timer, password, delay, random-text, frozen, schedule, schedule-lead. A rule's optional leadMinutes freezes settings in [start - lead, start) without forcing blocking; the lead reason's `until` is the underlying window end so the lock never shortens at the real start. Delay and random-text are whole-gate LWW operations: newer releases beat stale arms, newer arms beat old releases, equal stamps keep armed/reset/longer states, and legacy peers without the new fields cannot erase active gates. Merge cases carry an optional `now` (default 0): the schedule rule asks whether exactly one side is settings_locked at merge time — with fixture stamps in the small thousands, an active timer/frozen/password means locked. The password is a timestamped arm/unlock tombstone CRDT (greater passwordTs wins; a tie keeps an armed hash over a cleared one, and two armed hashes keep the lexicographically smaller); schedules are last-writer-wins EXCEPT that a locked side's list beats an unlocked peer regardless of stamps. passwordTs and schedulesUpdatedAt are clamped to `now` by sanitize (never now+maxLockMs): both order last-writer-wins merges, so forged future stamps must never be admitted. Same-id rules at equal schedule stamps resolve by a canonical content string that includes the tz pin and valid lead time, so two same-id rules pinned to different zones still converge deterministically. Scoped merge overlays every currently-active rule from both peers on the normal whole-list winner; once no rule is active, ordinary scoped protected/LWW/deletion policy applies. Accepted scoped lists have unique IDs. Merge-ordering metadata stamps accept only safe nonnegative integers (fractions sanitize to 0), and rule/ID canonical ordering uses UTF-8 bytes in both languages.
